question_set.question: Using highlight_region_by_value, how do the corners of the race × education grid appear after applying the specified highlighting, and which cell appears weak compared to its neighbors?

answer.value: A 70-point floor knocks most of group A into the background while leaving a constellation of brighter cells around group E and group D, especially where parental education reaches bachelor’s or master’s levels (group E tops out near 80 on that master’s cell). The awkward neighbor is group B at the high-school education level: it dims more sharply than B’s associate’s or bachelor’s columns, so the eye catches a local trough there even as other groups still show mid‑70s pockets.

key_insights: Bright cells cluster toward higher parental education and skew toward groups D and E rather than spanning every race evenly.
Group B’s high-school column is a visible low point relative to B’s other education stacks.

reasoning_trace.rationale: Dims low scores so strong cells and anomalies stand out without recomputing aggregates by hand.
